issues.legal_issue: A widow may succeed jointly with a son to hereditary shebaitship under the Hindu law of succession as modified by legislation giving widows a son's share in a deceased Hindu's property.
material_facts: The endowment deed provided that, after the founder's death and the death of his first wife, the founder's heirs would act as shebaits.
The first wife died before the founder, who later died leaving his second wife and his son alive.
The shebait was entitled to remuneration equal to a share of the endowed property's net income.
The case concerned succession to shebaitship after the founder's death, and the widow claimed a joint right with the son.
issues.conclusion: The widow was entitled to joint shebaitship with the son. Shebaitship is property for this purpose, and the Hindu Women's Rights to Property Act does not exclude it from its operation.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2 and 3(1) of the Hindu Women's Rights to Property Act, 1937, as amended, give a widow the same share as a son when a Hindu governed by the Dayabhaga school dies intestate; section 3(3) makes the widow's interest a limited Hindu woman's estate, and section 5 addresses when a person is deemed to die intestate. Shebaitship combines an office and duties with a beneficial or proprietary interest, and ordinarily follows the line of inheritance unless the founder directs otherwise or a different custom is proved: Vidya Varuti v. Balusami; Manohar Mukherji v. Bhupendra Nath Mukherji; Ganesh Chunder Dhur v. Lal Behary; Bhabatarini v. Ashalata; and Gossamee Sree Greedharreejee v. Rumanlolljee Gossamee. Umayal Achi v. Lakshmi Achi concerned trust management without an established beneficial interest and did not establish a general exclusion of shebaitship; the distinction is consistent with P. Suryanarayanacharyulu v. P. Seshamma. Anuragi Kuer v. Paramanand supports the principle that a female successor's shebait interest devolves after her death to the heirs of the last male holder.

rule.if: shebaitship_succession_dispute and shebait_has_beneficial_interest and male_shebait_died_intestate and widow_and_son_survived

predicates.shebaitship_succession_dispute: The proceeding concerns who succeeds to a hereditary shebaitship.
predicates.shebait_has_beneficial_interest: The holder of the shebaitship has a beneficial or proprietary interest connected with the endowed property.
predicates.male_shebait_died_intestate: The male holder died without an effective testamentary disposition governing the succession at issue.
predicates.widow_and_son_survived: The deceased holder was survived by a widow and a son who are eligible to succeed under the applicable succession law.

issues.definition: When a succession dispute concerns a shebaitship carrying a beneficial interest and a male holder dies intestate leaving a widow and son, the widow shares the shebaitship with the son.

issues.legal_issue: A deed that provides for shebaitship to devolve on the founder's heirs does not, merely by providing a separate appointment power in a specified contingency involving the absence of issue, limit the term heirs to issue.
material_facts: The deed provided for the founder's wife to act as shebait after him and then for the founder's heirs to act as shebaits.
A proviso permitted the founder to appoint a shebait in the specified contingency that he died without issue and without authorizing his wife to adopt.
The founder died leaving a son, so the contingency in the proviso did not arise.
The widow claimed shebaitship as an heir alongside the son.
issues.conclusion: The deed's reference to the founder's heirs bears its ordinary meaning and is not restricted to his issue; the proviso did not give issue priority in the circumstances because its stated contingency did not arise.
issues.legal_principle: The deed is read as a whole, giving the word heirs its ordinary meaning where the main clause does not restrict it, while treating the proviso as an exception applying to the contingency it specifies. The court rejected the argument that heirs meant only issue and relied on the approach to similar words of devolution in Umayal Achi v. Lakshmi Achi. The majority treated the proviso as an exception to the general succession direction; the separate concurrence considered that deed interpretation should not mechanically import technical rules governing statutory provisos, but agreed with the result.

predicates.hereditary_office_deed_provides_for_succ: The instrument governing a hereditary religious office directs that the founder's heirs succeed to the office.
predicates.deed_proviso_allows_appointment_only_if_: The instrument gives the founder an appointment power under a stated contingency that includes the founder having no issue.

issues.definition: Where an instrument directs succession to the founder's heirs and its appointment proviso depends on the founder leaving no issue, the heirs clause covers all persons entitled to inherit rather than only the founder's issue.
